what_constrained: Pebble 4 kB persistent storage and phone-only GPS required bounded watch history and optional location capture.
what_worked: Pure C score model, real Emery match replay, and independent verification exposed winning-point undo and save transaction gaps.
what_differently: Design the storage commit protocol before the first UI pass and test the capacity rollover path earlier.

what_constrained: The Pebble appstore requires a fresh UUID or existing owner mapping, Emery-sized screenshots, and a published release flag; physical watch and phone GPS checks remained open.
what_worked: Native screenshots, local PBW metadata inspection, a fresh release review, and public-page verification confirmed the VolleyKeeper 0.1.0 listing.
what_differently: Keep a prepared listing and store media beside the project before the next release, then validate the paired iPhone path on hardware.

what_constrained: A 200x228 watch display had to show set outcome, final points, court illustration, Next or Save, and Undo without changing persisted match data.
what_worked: Drawing the result from existing match state kept scoring logic intact; Emery replay exposed the need to retain save and GPS notices on the new screen.
what_differently: Capture realistic 25-23 and 23-25 result states earlier, then check touch and button actions before publishing screenshots.

what_constrained: The first set-result net occupied a thin boxed strip and looked like a fence at 200x228; the user expected the airy court hierarchy of the concept image.
what_worked: A light canvas, central score, perspective court lines, and sparse lighter net matched the visual direction while retaining native controls and team-color accents.
what_differently: Inspect a native-resolution result capture against the concept before publishing the first implementation.
